task.description:
Closing gate on WF03-ISS0204-20260821. DOC-UPDATER settled ISS-0204 (the `started_at` contradiction) in direction (a) -- ORCH stamps at dispatch -- and wrote a new canonical section, HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 1.2, replacing the rule text in section 1 step 3 and section 3's table row, with a four-line pointer added to ORCHESTRATOR.md section 6. Its report is `result` in `handoffs/WF03-ISS0204-20260821/step-03-settle-started-at.json`; read it there and treat it as a claim to be re-derived, not as evidence. The diff is `git show ef62d4b` (docs) and `git show b24edef` (handoff); both are committed locally and NOT pushed.

You are the only gate on this run -- there is no SECURITY-REVIEWER step (no tenant-data path, no code), no test step (no code under test), and no human backstop. A PASS here is what releases the queue task.

RE-DERIVE, do not read back. Each numbered item below names what you must run or open yourself:

1. THE MEASUREMENT IS THE LOAD-BEARING CLAIM AND IT IS QUOTED IN A PROTOCOL DOC AS REPRODUCIBLE. Run the command in section 1.2's fenced block yourself, verbatim, from the repo root, and compare every bucket against the numbers section 1.2 asserts: 606 files, 0 unparseable, 10 null `started_at`, and of the 596 remaining 468 at gap zero, 14 at 1-30s, 89 over 30s, 25 negative, of which 20 have a `created_at` on a round :00 minute. Note that the corpus GREW during this run (this run's own two handoff files are in it), so a small drift in `files` is expected and is not a discrepancy -- say what you got and whether it reconciles. A bucket that does not reconcile IS a discrepancy: report it.

2. CHECK THE INFERENCE, NOT ONLY THE ARITHMETIC. Section 1.2 argues from the 25 negative-gap files that the ORIGINAL rationale in section 1 step 3 named the wrong culprit -- that the corruption on disk is a fabricated ORCH `created_at`, not an agent-written `started_at`. Open at least two of those 25 files yourself and judge whether the round-:00-minute evidence actually supports that reading. If it does not, this is a FAIL: the whole direction rests on it.

3. NO DOCUMENT STILL STATES THE REJECTED RULE. Grep `started_at` across `docs/` and `.claude/` (excluding `handoffs/`) and read every hit. Section 1 step 3, section 3's table row, ORCHESTRATOR.md and core-directives.md must all be consistent with section 1.2 -- a leftover statement of 'ORCH only, immediately before dispatch' as a rule in its own right is the exact dead-text defect ISS-0204 was filed against, reproduced.

4. ONE CANONICAL STATEMENT, POINTERS ELSEWHERE (the issue's AC5). Judge whether ORCHESTRATOR.md section 6's addition is genuinely a pointer or is a second copy of the rule. Same question for section 1 step 3 and section 3's table row: they may point and may state the field's meaning, but they may not restate the procedure.

5. WEAK-MODEL EXECUTABILITY (the issue's AC2). Section 1.2's three-step procedure is now the only thing standing between a weak ORCH and the defect recurring. Read it as such an agent would: is each step mechanically executable without judgement, including the 'created but not immediately dispatched' branch? Name any step that requires an inference the text does not supply.

6. ISSUE CLOSURE. `docs/issues/ISS-0204.yaml` carries `status: resolved`, `resolved_in_run: WF03-ISS0204-20260821`, and a `resolved_at` that is plausibly a real clock read. Confirm GH#395 is actually closed with `gh issue view 395 --json state,closedAt` -- do not take the step report's word for it.

7. BOOKKEEPING AND SCOPE. `git show --stat ef62d4b b24edef`: nothing outside `docs/` and `handoffs/WF03-ISS0204-20260821/` may be touched, and no historical handoff file may have been backfilled to match the new rule. Both JSON files in this run's directory must parse under `json.loads`. `handoffs/orchestrator.log` and `handoffs/registry.json` are ORCH's, are deliberately still uncommitted in the working tree, and are not yours to touch -- confirm they have not SHRUNK (`git diff --numstat` deletions must be 0) and leave them alone.

8. This dispatch's own `started_at` was stamped by ORCH from the same clock read as `created_at`, which is the rule DOC-UPDATER just adopted, applied immediately. Confirm it, and confirm ORCH's spawn prompt for you did not ask you to stamp it. If either is false, that is a MINOR finding against ORCH and it belongs in `result.issues`.

VERDICT: PASS or FAIL against the seven acceptance criteria on the Step 03 handoff plus the items above. A FAIL must name each failed criterion and the specific gap, per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL section 2's validator-fail example. Non-gating wording observations go in `result.issues` at MINOR -- ORCH files those as follow-on issues rather than reworking this run. Commit your own handoff file. Do not write `handoffs/registry.json` or `handoffs/orchestrator.log`, and do not edit `docs/` unless a FAIL is being avoided by a correction you are explicitly making -- in which case say so; you are a gate, not a producer.
acceptance_criteria: The section 1.2 measurement command was re-run first-hand from the repo root and every bucket is reported with your own numbers, with any drift from the asserted figures reconciled or flagged
At least two of the 25 negative-gap files were opened and the fabricated-created_at inference is judged on their actual contents, not on the step report's summary
Every `started_at` hit across docs/ and .claude/ outside handoffs/ was read, and the verdict states that none restates the rejected rule
The one-canonical-statement criterion is judged for HANDOFF_PROTOCOL section 1 step 3, section 3's table row, ORCHESTRATOR.md section 6 and core-directives.md by name
Section 1.2's three-step ORCH procedure is assessed for weak-model executability, with any judgement-requiring step named
GH#395's closed state was confirmed with gh directly, and ISS-0204.yaml's resolved fields were read from the file

git show --stat confirms no file outside docs/ and handoffs/WF03-ISS0204-20260821/ was committed and no historical handoff was backfilled; orchestrator.log and registry.json show 0 deletions and were not modified by this step
A PASS/FAIL verdict is recorded with the evidence for each check named, and this handoff file parses under json.loads

result.summary: PASS on all eight acceptance criteria. Every check re-derived first-hand; nothing taken from DOC-UPDATER's report. (1) MEASUREMENT RE-RUN VERBATIM from the repo root, the fenced python heredoc in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL S1.2 exactly as printed. My numbers: 607 files, 0 unparseable, 10 null started_at, 469 gap==0, 14 gap 1-30s, 89 gap>30s, 25 gap<0, of which 20 have a created_at on a round :00 minute. Asserted: 606/0/10/468/14/89/25/20. Drift is +1 file and +1 in the zero bucket ONLY, and it reconciles exactly: this run's own step-03b handoff (created_at and started_at both 2026-08-21T10:20:01Z, gap 0) did not exist at 10:18:05Z when DOC-UPDATER measured, and step-03 (null) already did. Every other bucket -- nulls, 1-30s, >30s, negatives, round-minute negatives -- matches to the unit. No discrepancy. Note for a future re-runner: the doc's figures are correct as of its own writing but will keep drifting upward in `files`/`gap==0` as the corpus grows; the text already flags the corpus as evidence, and I am not asking for a rewrite. (2) INFERENCE CHECKED ON THE FILES, NOT THE ARITHMETIC. I enumerated all 25 negative-gap files myself and opened three. The round-:00-minute evidence supports the fabricated-created_at reading, and more strongly than S1.2 argues, because a second independent signal is present that S1.2 does not use: in these files completed_at is ALSO earlier than created_at and sits coherently beside started_at. WF02-REQ051-20260818/step-06-doc-updater.json: created_at 23:00:00Z (round), started_at 19:29:00Z, completed_at 19:35:00Z -- the two agent-adjacent values form a sane 6-minute step while ORCH's created_at is 3.5h later. WF02-REQ054-20260819/step-06-doc-updater.json: created_at 06:05:00Z (round), started_at 04:41:48Z, completed_at 04:42:16Z, and the agent's own result.summary independently records the status-history event it appended at 2026-08-19T04:41:48Z -- an external corroboration of the non-round value against a different file. A third, WF02-REQ054-20260819/step-02c-security-reviewer.json (created 04:10:00Z round, started 04:07:21Z, completed 04:07:51Z), shows the same shape. Round-minute-with-zero-seconds on the ORCH field vs. second-resolution on the agent-adjacent fields is exactly the drift signature docs/anti-patterns.md's 'Extrapolating handoff timestamps instead of reading the clock (ORCH)' records first-hand. The inference holds; the receiving agents are exonerated. (3) NO DOCUMENT STILL STATES THE REJECTED RULE. Grepped `started_at` across docs/ and .claude/ (.claude/: zero hits) and read every hit. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL S1 step 3 (L31-35), S1.2 (L78-166), S2's schema stub (L185, type only), S3 prose (L470, monotonicity only) and S3's table row (L475), S4.1's reconstruction list (L709-710: 'started_at is not on this list and is not rewritten: ORCH already stamped it at dispatch' -- consistent with (a), would have contradicted (b)), ORCHESTRATOR.md L162-167, core-directives.md L447 (monotonicity only, no ownership claim), anti-patterns.md L87-112 and L1072 (historical narrative, and it already attributes created_at/started_at stamping to ORCH -- consistent), ISS-0196.yaml L46 ('alongside the started_at rule ORCH already owns' -- consistent), ISS-0204.yaml, and one unrelated hit (docs/status/REQ-023-release-2026-08-16.yaml L120, a database column of the same name in instance_projections, not this field). NOWHERE does the rejected formulation 'ORCH only, immediately before dispatch' survive as a rule in its own right. The dead-text defect is not reproduced. (4) ONE CANONICAL STATEMENT, POINTERS ELSEWHERE -- judged by name for all four. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL S1 step 3: POINTER. It states ownership and the agent-facing prohibition (which is that section's job -- it is the claim procedure) and explicitly says 'Nothing about it is restated here'; it carries no clock read, no write ordering, no measurement. S3's table row: POINTER, and the row must say something in its 'When' column or the table has a hole; 'at dispatch -- same write and same clock read as created_at, per S1.2' is the minimum that makes the row readable and it defers for the rest. ORCHESTRATOR.md S6: POINTER, and it follows the form of the S2-pointer paragraph immediately above it in the same file (bold lede naming the rule, then 'this line does not restate it' plus the cross-reference) -- consistent with the file's existing convention rather than an ad-hoc second copy. core-directives.md: UNTOUCHED and correctly so; its only mention is the completed_at monotonicity constraint, which is a different rule and was already there. AC5 met: one canonical home, three pointers, no third copy. (5) WEAK-MODEL EXECUTABILITY of S1.2's three steps. Steps 1 and 3 are fully mechanical: take one clock read using S3's named command; do not put a started_at instruction in the spawn prompt. Step 2's main path is mechanical (write both fields from that one value in the file-creating write). Its 'created but not immediately dispatched' branch is executable and, importantly, FAIL-SAFE either way -- a weak ORCH that never notices the branch writes created_at==started_at, and one that always re-reads at spawn writes started_at>=created_at; neither can produce the negative-gap class, which is the property the whole direction was chosen for. Two judgement-requiring points named, neither gating, both filed below as MINOR: (a) 'genuinely create a handoff you do not dispatch immediately' has no threshold, so the branch condition is a judgement call (harmless, per the fail-safe above); (b) a real gap -- S1 step 3 tells the receiving agent to report a null started_at 'so ORCH fixes the dispatch', but S1.2's last paragraph says the null files stay as they are and are not backfilled, and no step tells ORCH what 'fix' means for a handoff already in an agent's hands. A weak ORCH reading both has no mechanical action. (6) ISSUE CLOSURE confirmed at source, not from the report. `gh issue view 395 --json state,closedAt` returns state CLOSED, closedAt 2026-08-21T10:17:57Z. docs/issues/ISS-0204.yaml read directly: status: resolved (L42), resolved_in_run: WF03-ISS0204-20260821 (L43), resolved_at: 2026-08-21T10:16:41Z (L44) -- second-resolution, not a round minute, and it precedes both the GH close (10:17:57Z) and the docs commit (15:17:44+05:00 = 10:17:44Z) in a coherent order, so it reads as a real clock read rather than a fabrication. (7) BOOKKEEPING AND SCOPE. `git show --stat --name-only ef62d4b b24edef` lists exactly four paths: docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md, docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md, docs/issues/ISS-0204.yaml, handoffs/WF03-ISS0204-20260821/step-03-settle-started-at.json. Nothing outside docs/ and this run's handoff directory; no lib/, priv/, test/ or web/. NO HISTORICAL HANDOFF BACKFILLED -- the only handoff path in either commit is this run's own, added as a new file (83 insertions, 0 deletions), and my own re-run found the 25 negative-gap and 10 null files still uncorrected on disk, which is the positive evidence that the corpus was left as evidence. `git diff --numstat` on the two ORCH-owned files: handoffs/orchestrator.log 8 insertions / 0 deletions, handoffs/registry.json 21 insertions / 0 deletions -- append-only intact, zero deletions on both. (The step report quoted 6/0 for the log; it is now 8/0 because ORCH has appended since. Growth, not shrinkage.) Neither file was read-modified or staged by me; both remain ' M' uncommitted for ORCH. Both JSON files under handoffs/WF03-ISS0204-20260821/ parse under json.loads, this one included, verified after writing this result. (8) THIS DISPATCH'S OWN started_at. Confirmed compliant: created_at and started_at are both 2026-08-21T10:20:01Z -- identical to the second, i.e. one clock read, one write, exactly S1.2 step 2's main path, applied by ORCH on the first dispatch after adopting it. ORCH's spawn prompt for me said 'Claim it by setting `status` to `IN_PROGRESS` -- nothing else', which is S1.2 step 3 honoured verbatim: it did not ask me to stamp started_at. Both halves true, so no MINOR against ORCH on this item. IDIOM/SCOPE NOTES for my standing remit: docs-only run, no Elixir, no gen_statem, no supervision tree and no tenant-data path touched, so items 1-3 of the REVIEWER charter do not apply. On scope creep (item 4): the change is proportionate -- one new subsection plus two rewritten clauses plus a four-line pointer, no new protocol machinery, no linter and no schema change invented ahead of need (the linter idea is correctly left parked on ISS-0191 rather than built here). No decision record is contradicted. GATE VERDICT: PASS. Queue task 204 is released.

issues.description: S1.2 step 2's exception branch ('if you genuinely create a handoff you do not dispatch immediately, re-read the clock and overwrite started_at') gives no threshold for 'immediately', so the branch condition is a judgement call for a weak ORCH. Non-gating because the rule is fail-safe in both readings: taking the branch yields started_at > created_at, skipping it yields started_at == created_at, and neither can produce the negative-gap class. A one-clause threshold ('if more than a few minutes pass between creating the file and spawning the agent') would remove the judgement entirely.

Unclosed loop between S1 step 3 and S1.2's last paragraph. Step 3 tells the receiving agent to leave a null started_at alone and report it at MINOR 'so ORCH fixes the dispatch', but S1.2's last paragraph rules that null files stay as they are and are not backfilled, and no step tells ORCH what 'fix' means for a handoff already in an agent's hands. A weak ORCH receiving that MINOR has no mechanical action to take. Suggest one sentence in S1.2 stating the intended resolution -- most likely 'do not backfill it; fix the NEXT dispatch' -- since that is what actually happened on this run and it is currently only inferable.

S1.2's corpus figures ('606 files ... 468 ...') are asserted as a reproducible measurement in a document whose reader is invited to re-run the command, but two of the buckets grow every time a handoff is written -- my re-run three minutes later already returned 607 and 469. Accurate as of writing and correctly attributed to a date, but a later reader will read a mismatch as a defect. Suggest 'as of 2026-08-21, and the file and zero-gap counts grow with the corpus; the shape of the distribution is the finding, not the absolute counts' next to the figures.

Your dispatch of this handoff already complied with the new S1.2 rule -- keep doing that.
